:::{#thm-risk-decomposition}
#### Squared-error risk decomposition

Let $g^*(X) \eqdef \E{Y \mid X}$.
For any prediction function $g(X)$ with $\E{g(X)^2} < \infty$:

$$\popriskf{g} = \popriskf{g^*} + \E{\sqf{g(X) - g^*(X)}}$$

:::

::: proof

The steps use
the [squared-error risk](#def-squared-error-risk) definition,
@lem-prediction-error-split,
and @lem-cross-term-zero:

$$
\ba
\popriskf{g}
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_g}}
&& \text{(definition of the squared-error risk)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_{g^*} + \paren{g(X) - g^*(X)}}}
&& \text{(the prediction error splits at } g^* \text{)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_{g^*}}} + 2 \cd \E{\prederr_{g^*}\paren{g(X) - g^*(X)}} + \E{\sqf{g(X) - g^*(X)}}
&& \text{(expand the square; linearity of expectation)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\prederr_{g^*}}} + 2 \cd 0 + \E{\sqf{g(X) - g^*(X)}}
&& \text{(the cross term is } 0 \text{)} \\
&= \popriskf{g^*} + \E{\sqf{g(X) - g^*(X)}}
&& \text{(definition of the squared-error risk of } g^* \text{)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-risk-decomposition}
#### The risk decomposition in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
the constant prediction $g_1(X) = 3$ has risk $\popriskf{g_1} = 5$,
which @thm-risk-decomposition splits as $5 = 1 + 4$:
the risk $1$ of the conditional mean plus the excess $4$ from using $g_1$.

:::
